newsitem.title: USA: W. African crude eclipses Brent on U.S. Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: W. African crude eclipses Brent on U.S. Gulf Coast.

text.p: A variety of West African grades eclipsed Brent and other North Sea crudes on the Gulf Coast on Wednesday amid scattered buying, traders said.
The spread between bellwethers West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent for April was around $1.40-45 cents a barrel, down 10-20 cents from Tuesday afternoon.
The narrowing arbitrage apparently dissuaded some North Sea sellers.
"I don't think there are a whole lot of (North Sea) barrels coming over here," one trader said.
Plenty of West African crude was still available, although traders said some Brass River and Qua Iboe were picked up for early April arrival. No price was indicated.
Qua Iboe was last heard done at a discount of 20 cents to WTI/Cushing.
Bonny Light was last heard at April WTI plus 50 cents a barrel for early April.
In Latin America, Colombian Cano Limon remained abundant after Exxon cut back on spot purchases for its Baton Rouge refinery, traders said.
The crude was assessed around $2.50 a barrel under April WTI for loading in March.

A top official at Colombia's state-owned Ecopetrol denied reports that Cano Limon's quality had deteriorated. He downplayed Exxon's cutback, saying that the U.S. major still had a term contract for Cano Limon.
Overall, Gulf Coast demand was seen picking up. "(Refiners) are lurking in the wings waiting for the opportunity to pounce" for early April barrels, one Texas trader said.
